scope: Read-only GitHub primary-source review of Yehu Chen repository snapshots, row structure, and AZ2012/MO2016 data correspondences; no fitting or target admission.

repository.author: Yehu Chen (GitHub account yahoochen97; README contact chenyehu@wustl.edu)
repository.readme_claim: Forecasting U.S. 2020 Senate Election; says distributed under MIT License and points to LICENSE.
repository.license_caveat: Raw LICENSE at the inspected commit returned 404; recursive Git tree had no repository-root LICENSE; GitHub repository API reported license=null. Dataset rights remain unclear; local captures only.
repository.commit_signature: The relevant commits are not established as signed/authenticated timestamps; GitHub API commit objects show author timestamps and immutable commit IDs.

snapshots.name: later-2018-snapshot-metadata-only
snapshots.timing: Post-2020 election; not a pre-2020 data vintage.

generated_2018_2020_code.behavior: Reads FiveThirtyEight current Senate poll CSV; creates candidate-level rows; computes support as samplesize*pct//100; computes daysLeft via negative inclusive date_range(start_date,election_date); removes start/end dates, candidate percentage, name and party; subsequent handling refers to poll_id/question_id.
generated_2018_2020_code.limitation: Script only documents generating 2018 and 2020 data, not legacy CNNdata1992-2016.csv; do not apply its date/count semantics to legacy rows as established fact.

candidate_rows.assessment: Strong content/source-row candidate: exact pollster, state/cycle/candidates, N and support counts triangulate with primary release and 538. Yet Chen has no poll ID/question/link; Tierney has no row-source ID, population, start, question or unique sample ID. N=470 in Tierney is the two-party count sum, not primary total N. Same questionnaire/respondents not proven.

Chen 750/341/335 record strongly content-matches Emerson's later Nov 4-5 poll, not the Oct 28-31 n650 poll. Tierney's D/R support counts equal Chen's candidate-level numberSupport but its endDate Oct 30 conflicts with Nov 4-5; Tierney n=676 is the D/R sum rather than N750. No question/sample identifier/crosswalk establishes that Tierney row is the later survey. Leave ambiguous, do not join.

chen_paper.title: Polls, Context, and Time: A Dynamic Hierarchical Bayesian Forecasting Model for US Senate Elections
chen_paper.data_source: Paper states Senate polling data came from CNN and FiveThirtyEight; acknowledges Harry Enten at CNN for providing data.

tierney_paper.title: Bias and Excess Variance in Election Polling: A Not-So-Hidden Markov Model
tierney_paper.data_chain: Article relies on Chen et al. Senate dataset for its 1992-2020 Senate analysis; supports collection-level lineage, not poll-row identity.

handling_note: During setup, initial `head -3` inspection of the 2019 CNNData2018.csv printed its first two poll rows, including the outcome-share field. Those outcome values are intentionally not reproduced or used in this analysis. No other 2018 row values were inspected.
conclusion: Author archive exact candidate-count matches materially strengthen the Tierney/Chen data-row candidate linkage. Exact sample/question identity remains unproven because row identifiers and question/source crosswalks are absent and MO date conflicts with the likely original release.
